---
id: dec-0004
kind: decision
title: Execution status is derived from kazi at read time, never stored in the ledger
state: accepted
created: "2026-07-29T20:00:00Z"
tags: [founding, kazi-seam, status]
edges:
  - type: derives_from
    to: int-0003
    note: storing status would make dira a tracker, which is the tool being deleted
alternatives:
  - option: Store planned/in-progress/done/blocked as a state field on entries
    why_not: >
      A hand-entered status field is precisely what went stale in Obsidian and
      Linear. It is correct at the moment of writing and wrong within a day, and
      the wrongness is invisible. A derived view cannot lie: if the join says
      converged, kazi converged it.
    revisit_if: never for hand-entry; a cached snapshot with a visible staleness timestamp is acceptable
  - option: Have dira poll kazi and write status back into entry files
    why_not: >
      This is the stale-field problem with extra steps, and it makes every status
      change a git commit — flooding the history that dec-0002 exists to keep
      readable.
  - option: Let kazi own the whole picture and not derive anything
    why_not: >
      kazi groups by goal and can only see work that has a goal. The two buckets
      that hurt most — "decided but never planned" and "blocked on an unanswered
      question" — exist upstream of any goal, so kazi structurally cannot report
      them. That gap is the reason dira exists.
source:
  hook: manual
  tier: human
confirmed_by: human
---

dira owns **ledger** states (accepted, open, active). kazi owns **run** states.
Every bucket a human asks for is the join of the two across `realized_by` edges,
computed at read time:

| Bucket | Join rule |
|---|---|
| To be planned | accepted decision or active intent with **no** `realized_by` edge |
| Planned | `realized_by` points at an approved proposal or an unapplied goal |
| In progress | linked goal has a live run in kazi |
| Completed | linked goal converged; kazi's evidence is attached by reference |
| Execution-blocked | kazi reports the linked goal stuck or over-budget |
| Decision-blocked | an **open question** with a `blocks` edge gating this entry |

The last row is the one only dira can produce, and it is the load-bearing one:
work stalled because a human never answered a question does not appear in any
execution tracker, because no goal was ever created to be stalled.

Two invariants follow. First, dira **never asserts doneness** — it inherits it,
so "done" stays as objective as kazi's predicates make it. Second, when kazi is
absent or errors, dira degrades to the ledger-side buckets (to-be-planned,
decision-blocked, achieved/abandoned intents) and says so, rather than filling the
gap with a guess.
